brief.subject: Q3 report
brief.email:
Hi,

Here’s the Q3 report. The headline: a solid quarter overall, but with a few areas we need to get ahead of before year end.

## Overall
• Revenue £4.2m, up 8% on Q2 and 3% ahead of plan
• Gross margin steady at 41%
• Customer retention 94%, our best quarter this year

## Regional highlights
• North: our strongest region, up 14%, driven by two new enterprise contracts
• South: up 6%, with the new partner channel now 20% of sales
• Midlands: flat, but the Q4 pipeline looks healthier

## Areas of concern
• Scotland is down 9% after losing the Harper account; we need a recovery plan
• Delivery costs rose 12%, mostly fuel and the new courier contract
• Support response times slipped from 4 to 7 hours in September

## Follow-up actions
• Review the Scotland recovery plan before the board meeting
• Agree a cap on delivery costs with procurement
• Approve two temporary support hires for Q4

Could you take a look and let me know what you think, ideally before Friday’s board meeting?

Thanks,
Sam

trap.caveat: A well-known trap for earlier models. Many current models now answer correctly — as models change, old traps disappear and new ones emerge.

scaling.source: Parametric fit L(N, D) = E + A / N^alpha + B / D^beta from Hoffmann et al. (2022), 'Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models' (Chinchilla), arXiv:2203.15556. Constants are the refit by Besiroglu et al. (2024), 'Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt' (Epoch AI), arXiv:2404.10102, which found the original rounded values (E=1.69, A=406.4, B=410.7, alpha=0.34, beta=0.28) do not fit the paper's own data well. Loss is in nats per token.

compute.source: Standard approximations (Kaplan et al., 2020): training ≈ 6 × parameters × training tokens; generating ≈ 2 × parameters per token. Ignores hardware efficiency, attention overhead and long contexts.

popular.label: 100 billion tokens a day (a large public service)

usage.source: Illustrative conversation. Words-per-token is the common rule of thumb for English text; exact counts depend on the model's tokenizer. Relative input/output pricing reflects typical published API price lists, which change often — no specific prices are shown.

embedding.note: Token IDs and numbers are illustrative. Real models give each token a list of thousands of numbers.

meaning.note: Illustrative. Real embeddings have thousands of dimensions; this flattens them to two so they can be drawn.
